loops.minute_1: Click big cookie, earn 1 cookie per tap. Instant visual feedback (cookie shatters, particles). Audio: satisfying click. Goal: accumulate 13 cookies for first building (cursor). Why return: immediate power fantasy of automation unlocked.
loops.minute_10: First building (cursor) auto-generates 0.1 cookies/sec. Golden cookies appear randomly with temporary effects (2x production, +clicks). Economic decision: buy next cursor or save for first farm? Why return: production accelerating without clicks; next unlock is always visible and tantalizingly close.
loops.hour_5: 15+ buildings purchased. Passive income >90% of earnings. Sugar Lumps arrive (24h accumulation timegate). Wrinklers appear (click parasites that return digested cookies with interest). Why return: Sugar Lump ready for enhancement; Wrinkler cooldown cycling; new minigame unlocked (pet dragon Krumblor feeding). Progression never stalls.
loops.endgame: Ascension = voluntary reset for Heavenly Chips (prestige currency). Each prestige level = +1% CPS permanently. 637 achievements pace the endless grind. Grandmapocalypse narrative darkens UI, transforms visual style. Mini-games (garden, stock market) diversify interaction. Why return: ascension reset cycles create new strategic challenges; prestige scaling is infinite; meta-progression never stops.

objectives.player_goal: Maximize cookies per second (CPS) indefinitely; unlock all 637 achievements; reach highest ascension prestige possible. No formal endpoint.

games.retention_answer: Cookie Clicker retains players via infinite prestige scaling (each ascension unlocks harder challenges), visual escalation (Grandmapocalypse horror progression), and frequent unlocks (new buildings every 100-1000 cookies). The meta-loop (play→ascend→prestige grows→faster next run→repeat) replaces a missing endgame with a treadmill that feels rewarding because prestige multiplies early production exponentially. Periodic minigame integration breaks click monotony.

loops.minute_1: Open yard. Spend 5000 starting fish on one food bowl (basic). Audio: gentle tink. Yard is mostly empty. Why return: cats don't come instantly; curiosity about who arrives.
loops.minute_10: First cat arrives, eats food, leaves fish (10-100). Player taps to photograph (mementos). Cat departs after 20-60 min. Why return: see which cat arrived; try a different food combo to attract a new cat; take more photos for the album.
loops.hour_5: 10-15 distinct cats seen. Rare cat (special combo: specific food + furniture) begins emerging as hidden goal. Daily password reward (~500-2000 fish) makes return visits mandatory. Photo collection grows. Why return: completionist drive (how many cats exist?); password daily timegate; experimental fomo (seasonal cat may vanish).
loops.endgame: 86 total cats (including 26 rare variants). Seasonal events lock exclusive cats (e.g., snow event rare). Mementos collection = 250+ possible photos. No prestige or resetting. Why return: pure collection completion; seasonal exclusivity; rare cat hunts (specific furniture combos unlock rare variants only during seasons).

objectives.player_goal: Collect all 86 cats and their rare variants (26 additional rare forms); photograph all mementos (250+); complete seasonal events. No formal win condition; collection is indefinite.

games.retention_answer: Neko Atsume retains players via collection completion (86/86 cats is a visible progress bar), visual novelty (each cat has distinct art and personality), and temporal scarcity (seasonal events with exclusive rare cats). The soft timegate (cats visit unpredictably; password once per day) respects player time while encouraging daily return. Unlike Cookie Clicker's numeric infinity, Neko Atsume's collection has a measurable cap (86), making completion a reachable goal that nonetheless requires weeks of engagement. Zen audio-visual design (no alarm sounds, gentle purrs) reduces fatigue compared to click-heavy games.

visual_feedback: Particle burst on purchase/reward (numbers floating, coins/popcorn effect)
Progress bar or counter visible (achievements %, cats collected %, cookies/sec display)
Color escalation as difficulty/prestige grows (Cookie Clicker: milk % darkens bg; Neko: unlock new cat portraits)
Building/cat artwork distinct so each unlock feels visually earned
audio_feedback: Click sound per interaction (satisfying, not fatiguing)
Chime or jingle for milestone/rare discovery
Soft background music (Neko Atsume zen) or dynamic score escalation (Cookie Clicker Grandmapocalypse)
monotony_risks: Endless clicking without automation → mitigation: passive production unlocks early
Boring wait loops → mitigation: random events (Golden Cookies, rare cat spawns) break routine
Invisible progress → mitigation: always show growth metric (CPS, collection %), always have next unlock visible
Decision fatigue → mitigation: simple heuristics (buy cheapest building per ratio, try all cat foods) make meta-loops tractable
